title: Sensor failures in the first year
intro:
A water utility installs **15** flow sensors on its network. Each sensor fails in its first year with probability **0.08**, independently of the others. Let X be the number that fail in the first year.

Find the probability that exactly 2 fail, the probability that more than 2 fail, and the mean and standard deviation of X. Give the probabilities to three decimals or more.

Exactly.says: You left out C(15, 2) = 105, the number of ways to choose which 2 of the 15 sensors fail. Multiply by it.

MoreThan.says: That is P(X ≥ 2), "at least 2". "More than 2" starts at 3: 1 − [P(0) + P(1) + P(2)].

StandardDeviation.says: That is the variance, np(1 − p). The standard deviation is its square root.

hints: Check BINS: two outcomes, independent sensors, n = 15 fixed, the same p = 0.08 for each. So X ~ Binomial(15, 0.08).
"More than 2" is 1 − P(X ≤ 2) = 1 − [P(0) + P(1) + P(2)]. μ = np and σ = √(np(1 − p)).
